data.title: Feature Flag
data.tagline: A feature flag enables or disables a code path at runtime according to configuration or user conditions.
data.learningOutcome: You can tell when to expose a feature gradually by user scope and what portion of impact disabling a flag can stop.
data.description: The same deployed code can send employees to a new recommendation page while other people stay on the old path; closing the flag stops the new path on anomaly. It separates deploying code from deciding who gets a feature. Permanently deleting code or restoring a whole old version is not a feature flag itself.

learning.assumes: You know a new feature does not have to open to every user at once.
learning.outcome: You can tell when to expose a feature gradually by user scope and what portion of impact disabling a flag can stop.

distinctions.label: Rollback
distinctions.explanation: A Feature Flag controls which people enter a code path at runtime. A Rollback restores a system, configuration, or version to a known-good state.

distinctions.label: Quality Gate
distinctions.explanation: A Feature Flag controls access to code paths dynamically at runtime; a Quality Gate enforces test-passing and linting thresholds before code is merged or released.

explanation.title: Deployment and exposure can happen at different times
explanation.text: Code can already be deployed, while a flag sends only employees, a small group, or qualifying people to the new path. Observe real signals, then expand without waiting for another code release to control access.

explanation.title: Turning a flag off quickly stops one path
explanation.text: When new recommendations misbehave, turning off the flag returns people to the old path; monitoring, root-cause repair, and verification still follow. A flag does not repair data or restore a whole version.

data.boundary: A feature flag is not a version rollback. Disabling one normally stops only one feature path while other same-version changes keep running; rollback restores a whole prior version or configuration. It is also not permanent code deletion; retire unused flags after confirmation.

lessonPractice.title: The new recommendation page is deployed, but the team wants only employees to try it first and everyone to return to the old page immediately on error without redeploying. What fits best?

options.label: Add a feature flag for the new path, enable it only for employees, and disable it on anomaly
options.feedback: Correct. A flag controls who enters an already-deployed new path and can stop that path quickly.

options.label: Roll back the entire version whenever the trial audience needs adjustment
options.feedback: Rollback affects a whole version and cannot finely control who sees one feature in it.

options.label: Permanently delete old-page code first, then restore it if there is a problem
options.feedback: That removes the ability to return quickly to the old path and is not gradual exposure.

data.agentPrompt: Add a feature flag for the new recommendation page: enable it for employees only by default and keep other users on the old page. Monitor the new-path error rate after release; above threshold, disable the flag and confirm everyone returns to the old path without rolling back the entire version.
